title: Satellite monitoring is filling the time between displacement surveys, extending socioeconomic visibility while leaving verification and coverage limits open
source_unit: UNHCR Data Visualization Platform, From Space to Settlement: South Sudan socioeconomic monitoring between displacement surveys, September 2026
geography: Displacement-affected areas of South Sudan covered by UNHCR Forced Displacement Survey and Results Monitoring Survey locations

observations.period: September 2026; data continuity between displacement surveys

survey_gap.value: displacement settings can change faster than high-quality household surveys can be repeated

satellite_role.value: satellite estimates complement survey evidence by providing a more continuous view of where socioeconomic conditions may be shifting

operational_use.value: repeated estimates can flag locations for attention, contextual analysis, and field verification between survey rounds

observations.method: UNHCR SocioSat approach combining satellite imagery with Forced Displacement Survey and Results Monitoring Survey evidence, with validation and limitations documented in an accompanying paper.
observations.uncertainty: Satellite estimates are proxies and require local validation; they do not replace household surveys, administrative data, protection monitoring, or direct community feedback.
observations.subgroup: Refugees, internally displaced people, returnees, host communities, humanitarian operations, local authorities, and field-verification teams.
observations.counterinterpretation: More frequent spatial signals may improve targeting, but they can also create false precision or divert attention toward measurable places and away from less visible needs.

observations.period: 2023-2025; South Sudan survey baseline and repeated imagery

denominator.unit: years represented by 2023 survey baseline and 2024 and 2025 imagery

baseline.value: the 2023 Forced Displacement Survey provides a socioeconomic survey baseline

time_extension.value: imagery from 2024 and 2025 extends the picture beyond the survey year

change_detection.value: the model is intended to show where socioeconomic conditions may have moved between higher-quality survey rounds

open_stage.value: flagged change still requires contextual interpretation and field verification before operational or policy conclusions

observations.method: UNHCR comparison of survey-based estimates with satellite imagery across 2023-2025 in covered South Sudan locations.
observations.uncertainty: The time series is not a direct panel of the same households, and imagery-derived change can reflect multiple physical, social, environmental, or measurement processes.
observations.subgroup: Displacement-affected locations, communities living in and around camps, out-of-camp refugees, returnees, and host populations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Repeated imagery can make slow or missed deterioration visible, but it cannot reveal the meaning, safety, coping, or priorities behind a spatial signal without human evidence.

denominator.unit: Admin-3 areas where UNHCR FDS and RMS data were collected

coverage.value: analysis covers locations within the Admin-3 levels where FDS and RMS data were collected

included_settings.value: formal camp areas, refugees living outside camps, and surrounding host communities are included

exclusion.value: results represent covered displacement-affected areas and not the entire country

place_route.value: spatial monitoring can connect displacement, settlement conditions, host-community pressure, infrastructure, and service targeting

observations.method: UNHCR spatial analysis constrained to survey-covered Admin-3 areas and displacement-affected settings.
observations.uncertainty: Coverage boundaries limit national inference; formal and informal settlements, mobile populations, and places without survey baselines may be underrepresented.
observations.subgroup: Camp and non-camp displaced populations, returnees, host communities, local authorities, and humanitarian service providers in covered areas.
observations.counterinterpretation: Restricting the model to survey-covered areas can improve calibration, even while leaving broader populations outside the monitoring frame.

observations.period: 2026; humanitarian data governance and operational accountability

complementarity.value: satellite estimates, survey evidence, field verification, and programme monitoring are complementary rather than interchangeable

decision_route.value: the useful chain is signal, contextual analysis, verification, operational decision, and later monitoring

accountability_question.value: people affected by displacement should remain visible as communities with priorities and rights, not only as remotely inferred spatial indicators

next_test.value: join imagery signals to services, shelter, livelihoods, prices, protection, community feedback, and response timing

observations.method: Cross-source interpretation of UNHCR’s SocioSat, survey, validation, and operational-use framing.
observations.uncertainty: The public product does not establish the accuracy or effect of any specific intervention triggered by satellite monitoring.
observations.subgroup: Displaced people, host communities, humanitarian agencies, governments, donors, data scientists, and field staff.
observations.counterinterpretation: Remote sensing can protect scarce field capacity and improve early warning when used transparently, with consent-sensitive practice and meaningful community verification.

related_sources.claim: UNHCR displacement statistics methodology provides complementary definitions and population-count context.
UNHCR Global Trends provides complementary global displacement totals and return context.

boundary: This record adds a displacement-data continuity route from satellite monitoring through socioeconomic change detection, place targeting, field verification, and operational accountability. It is not respondent-level data, a household panel, a national estimate for South Sudan, proof of causal service effects, or a replacement for community feedback and direct protection evidence.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official UNHCR Data Visualization Platform product page was reviewed for the SocioSat purpose, FDS and RMS complementarity, South Sudan 2023-2025 time extension, Admin-3 coverage, camp and host-community inclusion, and field-verification limitations.
